title: Butternut Squash Soup

items: 1 medium butternut squash (2½–3 lb), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes (about 6 cups)
⅛ tsp ground nutmeg or ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
½ cup heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk

steps: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and ½ tsp of the salt and cook 5–7 min, stirring, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Add the squash, broth, the remaining ½ tsp salt, the pepper and the nutmeg or cinnamon. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, partly cover and simmer 20–25 min, until a squash cube crushes easily against the side of the pot with a fork.

Turn off the heat. Blend with an immersion blender 1–2 min, until completely smooth. With a countertop blender, fill it no more than halfway, take out the center cap of the lid, cover the hole with a folded towel and blend in batches. Hot soup can blow a sealed lid off.

Return the soup to the pot over low heat. Stir in the cream or coconut milk and warm 2–3 min without letting it boil. Taste and add salt. If it's too thick, thin with broth or water a few Tbsp at a time.
Ladle into bowls and top each with about 2 tsp pepitas.
tips: For deeper flavor, roast the squash first: toss the cubes with the oil and roast at 425°F for 25–30 min, until browned at the edges. Then simmer with the broth just 10 min.
Pre-cut squash skips the hardest step. You need about 2 lb (6 cups) of cubes.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze up to 3 months, ideally before adding the cream. Reheat in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring, until steaming. Add the pepitas when you serve.
